scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): backs independent judgment while insisting officials respect the public will; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Citizens elect officials to serve them, yet also trust those officials to think for themselves.
Some people argue that government officials should rely on their own judgment rather than unquestioningly carry out the will of the people they serve.
I agree that officials must use their judgment, but I believe they cannot simply ignore the wishes of the public.
First, officials often must follow their own judgment instead of public opinion alone.
Ordinary citizens cannot study every issue closely, while officials have access to experts and facts.
For example, a brief public panic might call for a harmful policy that a careful leader knows to avoid.
This shows that wise judgment can protect a nation from its own passing fears.
Officials must also sometimes defend unpopular groups whom the majority would gladly ignore.
A leader who only follows the polls may drop every principle when the mood changes.
To this extent, independent judgment is a necessary part of leadership.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why the public will must be respected

sentences.text: Second, however, officials cannot simply override the will of the people they were chosen to serve.
In a democracy, their power flows from the citizens and is meant to represent them.
Consider an official who ignores the clear and repeated wishes of the public, sure that he knows best.
Such arrogance can slide into a rule that no longer answers to anyone at all.
Leaders who lose touch with the people also lose the trust that makes government work.
The voice of the public, shown through votes, is a vital check on those in power.
Good officials, then, must balance their own judgment against the will of the people.
In conclusion, officials should use their judgment, especially to resist panic and protect the weak.
But ignoring the will of the people would betray the purpose of democratic government.
The wisest officials blend sound judgment with genuine respect for those they serve.
